q: Do we still need someone at the media desk?
a: Yes, and their job gets easier. Hearken suggests; the operator decides. Only references it’s very sure of can go up by themselves, and only if you turn that on.

Any recent Mac, Windows or Linux laptop. Faster computers, such as Apple Silicon Macs or PCs with a graphics card, can also use the extra-accurate models.

q: A verse wasn’t detected. What can we do?
a: Check the level meter moves when the pastor speaks, add names and words to listen for under Accuracy, and put the day’s readings in the Plan tab so they’re ready and recognised faster.
Open Accuracy and choose Automatic, then stop and start listening. A larger model that’s too slow for the computer is skipped automatically; the panel warns you if you’ve chosen one.
Some Android phones can’t open .local addresses. The QR code always works, and the Share panel shows a number address to type instead. Phones must be on the same Wi‑Fi as the laptop.

q: The phone remote asks for a PIN.
a: The PIN is shown in the Share panel on the media desk. It changes each time Hearken starts, so only people in the room can use the remote.

q: macOS says it can’t verify the developer.
a: Open System Settings → Privacy & Security and click Open Anyway. You only need to do this the first time.
